doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: How Saffire came together by chance
summary: A persistent guitar student and a third player led to three women playing together by accident, and there were no similar bands then.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: How did the idea for Saffire come about?

There was no idea. It was totally random. There was this woman who used to come up to me at shows and say she wanted me to teach her guitar. And I said, you know what? You want to learn guitar? Go over here this guy gives lessons or this gal gives lessons. And they know what they’re doing, so take lessons from them. And three years she hounded me. And I finally said fine. And I gave her lessons and she learned very quickly. I mean she learned very quickly as much as she wanted to learn and then she started doing an occasional job, started doing some things with another accompanist, another guitar player, and occasionally I would call her for a job or she’d call me for a job and we’d do something together. And then one day there was a room that I think they called her, I guess it was her, and they wanted, you know it was a big room. And she felt that, or I felt that we needed another person. And so we asked this woman who I was teaching a class, nothing to do with music in, this was during, well it’s a long story, during an era when I was putting my daughter through college so I was doing some non-musical things. So she joined us for that one gig. And they asked us back. And then other people asked us back. And they kept asking us back. It was totally random. The fact that we were all women was totally random, you know, there was no thought involved at all, at least not on my part, and I don’t think it was on anybody’s part. But it ended up being very successful.
It wasn’t, obviously then it wasn’t a contrived — gee if we had a group with three women we’ll be able to get more gigs.

Yeah, or a black, a Jew and — no. That did not happen. I love it that people say that we were that smart but we weren’t. But the truth was is that there were, at that time, you know, no other bands like us. Now there are others. You know there’s Three Bitchin’ Babes and there’s another one that’s named after a jewel, rubies or something. But I mean there have been girl groups but not recently and not that played instruments. So I guess at one time there was the International Sweethearts of Rhythm but that was a long time ago. Remember that?
Yeah. That was a whole big band.
That was a big band, yeah.
